questions.explanation_english:
Section 16 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 outlines specific measures required of educational institutions to achieve true inclusive education. Section 16(vi) mandates that institutions must:
'make suitable modifications in the curriculum and examination system to meet the needs of students with disabilities such as extra time for completion of examination paper, facility of scribe or amanuensis, exemption from second and third language courses.'

Options A, B, and D represent exclusionary, discriminatory, and unlawful practices. options_english: Autism Spectrum Disorder
Dyslexia, dysgraphia, and dyscalculia
Intellectual disability and Down syndrome
Aphasia and hearing impairment
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2 of the Schedule to the RPwD Act, 2016, 'Specific Learning Disabilities' (SLD) is defined as a heterogeneous group of conditions wherein there is a deficit in processing language, spoken or written, that may manifest itself as a difficulty to comprehend, speak, read, write, spell, or to do mathematical calculations. It specifically includes conditions such as Dyslexia (reading difficulty), Dysgraphia (writing and fine motor expression difficulty), and Dyscalculia (arithmetical calculation difficulty). In school education, identifying SLD is essential for school administrators to implement CBSE examination concessions, provide scribes, offer compensatory time, and design individualized education plans (IEPs).

Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Most government scholarship schemes for socio-economically disadvantaged groups prescribe a minimum attendance benchmark (usually 75%) as a mandatory condition for annual renewal.
Reason (R): The primary policy intent behind welfare scholarships is to incentivize consistent classroom attendance and arrest dropout rates among marginalized student populations.
In the context of the statements above, which one of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) directly explains Assertion (A). Welfare scholarship schemes (such as Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarships for SC, ST, OBC, and minority students) are designed not merely as unconditional cash transfers, but as targeted educational retention instruments. To ensure that students remain actively integrated into formal education and achieve learning milestones, guidelines mandate that the beneficiary must maintain at least 75% attendance during the academic session. Failure to meet the attendance threshold leads to withholding or non-renewal of the scholarship. The reason for imposing this 75% attendance condition is precisely the statutory and administrative objective of curbing chronic absenteeism, discouraging child labor, preventing early dropouts, and fostering daily institutional participation.

questions.question_english: Article 15(4) permits the State to make special provisions for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens, or for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes. What does the term "enabling provision" mean in this constitutional context?
options_english: The State is strictly and constitutionally mandated to provide reservations across all sectors
The State is empowered, but not legally bound, to make special provisions
Only the Union Parliament holds authority to enact such laws, excluding State legislatures
Citizens possess an absolute fundamental right to demand affirmative action reservation
questions.explanation_english: In constitutional law, an 'enabling provision' confers discretionary power, authority, and legislative competence upon the State to take affirmative action measures without imposing an absolute, judicially enforceable duty or mandate to do so. Under Article 15(4), the State is empowered to make special provisions (such as quotas, lower eligibility cutoffs, fee exemptions, or scholarships) for the advancement of SCs, STs, and SEBCs. However, citizens do not possess an enforceable fundamental right to claim reservations, nor can the judiciary issue a writ of mandamus compelling the government to institute quotas. As affirmed by the Supreme Court in cases like Ajit Singh (II) (1999) and Mukesh Kumar v. State of Uttarakhand (2020), Articles 15(4) and 16(4) are enabling clauses; providing reservation lies within executive and legislative discretion based on quantifiable data of backwardness.
questions.explanation_hindi: संवैधानिक न्यायशास्त्र में 'समर्थकारी उपबंध' (enabling provision) का अर्थ है कि यह प्रावधान राज्य को सकारात्मक कार्रवाई (जैसे आरक्षण, पात्रता अंकों में छूट या छात्रवृत्तियां) करने की शक्ति और अधिकार प्रदान करता है, परंतु राज्य पर ऐसा करने की कोई कानूनी या न्यायिक रूप से बाध्यकारी अनिवार्यता नहीं थोपता। अनुच्छेद 15(4) के तहत राज्य SC, ST और सामाजिक व शैक्षणिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों (SEBCs) की उन्नति के लिए विशेष नियम बना सकता है, किंतु नागरिक न्यायालय से परमादेश (mandamus) रिट जारी करवाकर आरक्षण की मांग को मौलिक अधिकार के रूप में लागू नहीं करवा सकते। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने 'अजीत सिंह (II) (1999)' तथा 'मुकेश कुमार बनाम उत्तराखंड राज्य (2020)' जैसे मामलों में यह दोहराया है कि अनुच्छेद 15(4) और 16(4) समर्थकारी स्वरूप के हैं; आरक्षण लागू करना सरकार के नीतिगत विवेकाधिकार का विषय है न कि कोई संवैधानिक अनिवार्यता।

questions.question_english: In the context of assessing eligibility for Economically Weaker Section (EWS) reservation, which of the following statements is legally correct regarding the computation of 'family income'?
options_english: It includes only the net take-home salary of the primary earning head of the family
It includes gross income from all sources for the financial year prior to the year of application
It strictly excludes all earnings generated directly from agricultural activities
It is calculated strictly after deducting all applicable direct income tax liabilities
questions.explanation_english:
As per the Central Government rules governing EWS reservation (DoPT OM No. 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) dated 31.01.2019), the term 'income' is defined comprehensively:

1. Gross Annual Income: It refers to gross income (prior to tax deductions, provident fund deductions, or other personal deductions), NOT take-home or net salary.
2. All Sources Included: The income calculation encompasses earnings from all sources, including salary, agriculture, business, profession, and other income streams. Agricultural income is expressly included.
3. Relevant Timeframe: Income is evaluated for the 'financial year prior to the year of application' for the certificate (e.g., for an application made in 2024-25, the income of FY 2023-24 is assessed).
4. Aggregation of Family: The combined income of the candidate, their parents, spouse, siblings under 18, and children under 18 must be computed together.

questions.explanation_english: In constitutional jurisprudence established in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) and affirmed in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022), reservations in India are structured into two categories: Vertical reservations and Horizontal reservations. Vertical reservations are social compartmental reservations provided under Article 16(4) for SC, ST, and OBC, and under Article 16(6) (103rd Constitutional Amendment) for EWS. These vertical categories are mutually exclusive quotas. On the other hand, horizontal reservations (such as for PwBD, women, or ex-servicemen under Articles 16(1) and 15(3)) cut across each vertical compartment. Because EWS functions as an independent, mutually exclusive vertical compartment of up to 10% carved out of the general/unreserved pool rather than an interlocking horizontal overlay, Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) correctly explains why it is vertical.

Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): A school Principal cannot deny admission to a child with a benchmark disability solely on the ground of their disability.
Reason (R): Section 16 of the RPwD Act, 2016 mandates that all educational institutions funded or recognized by the appropriate government must provide inclusive education and admit children with disabilities without discrimination.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true, but (R) is false
(A) is false, but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the direct statutory justification and correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Section 16 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 provides that the appropriate government and local authorities shall ensure that all educational institutions funded or recognized by them provide inclusive education to children with disabilities. Sub-clause (i) of Section 16 specifically mandates that institutions must 'admit them without discrimination and provide education and opportunities for sports and recreation activities equally with others'.

Therefore, any refusal by a school principal or administrative authority to admit a student on the ground of disability is a direct violation of Section 16, attracting penal consequences under Section 89 and Section 91/92 of the Act. Hence, R correctly explains A.

questions.explanation_english: Under Article 341(1) of the Constitution of India, the President of India is authorized to specify the castes, races, or tribes, or parts of or groups within castes, races, or tribes, which shall for the purposes of the Constitution be deemed to be Scheduled Castes in relation to a State or Union Territory (after consultation with the Governor in the case of a State), by public notification. Once this initial Presidential Order is issued (such as the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950), Article 341(2) stipulates that only Parliament may by law include in or exclude from the list of Scheduled Castes specified in that notification. State Governments, Governors, or Commissions have no power to alter or amend the Presidential list on their own.

questions.question_english: According to Section 34 of the RPwD Act, 2016, what is the minimum percentage of vacancies mandated to be reserved for persons with benchmark disabilities in every Government establishment?
questions.explanation_english:
Section 34(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 provides:
'Every appropriate Government shall appoint in every Government establishment, not less than four per cent. of the total number of vacancies in the cadre strength in each group of posts meant to be filled with persons with benchmark disabilities...'

This statutory provision represents a landmark increase from the 3% quota originally prescribed under Section 33 of the erstwhile Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995. Note the distinction: employment reservation under Section 34 is 4%, whereas reservation in higher education under Section 32 is 5%.

questions.question_english: A Principal of a newly constructed Delhi Government school notices that while there are ramps, they are too steep for a student to independently navigate a wheelchair, thereby violating accessibility norms. What is the standard recommended gradient for an accessible ramp in public buildings?
questions.explanation_english: According to the 'Harmonised Guidelines and Space Standards for Barrier Free Built Environment' notified under the RPwD Act, 2016 and the National Building Code of India (NBC), the standard recommended maximum gradient for a ramp in public buildings and schools is 1:12 (1 unit of vertical rise for every 12 units of horizontal run, representing an 8.33% slope). Steeper ramps (such as 1:8 or 1:10) create severe safety risks, including the danger of manual wheelchairs tipping backwards or slipping. The guidelines also stipulate that a ramp must have a minimum width of 1200 mm to 1500 mm, continuous handrails on both sides at 750 mm and 900 mm heights, a non-slip surface, and level landings of at least 1500 mm × 1500 mm every 9 metres of run.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 के अधीन अधिसूचित 'बाधा-मुक्त निर्मित परिवेश हेतु समेकित दिशा-निर्देश' तथा राष्ट्रीय भवन निर्माण संहिता (NBC) के अनुसार, सार्वजनिक भवनों एवं विद्यालयों में रैंप के लिए मानक अनुशंसित अधिकतम ढलान 1:12 (प्रत्येक 12 इकाई क्षैतिज दूरी पर 1 इकाई ऊर्ध्वाधर उठान, अर्थात 8.33% प्रवणता) है। 1:12 से अधिक तीव्र ढलान (जैसे 1:8 या 1:10) पर व्हीलचेयर चलाना अत्यंत जोखिम भरा होता है और उपयोगकर्ता के पीछे पलटने का खतरा रहता है। इसके अतिरिक्त, मानकों के अनुसार रैंप की चौड़ाई न्यूनतम 1200 से 1500 मिमी होनी चाहिए, दोनों किनारों पर 750 मिमी व 900 मिमी की ऊंचाई पर दोहरी रेलिंग (हैंडरेल) होनी चाहिए, तथा प्रत्येक 9 मीटर की दौड़ के बाद 1500 मिमी × 1500 मिमी का समतल लैंडिंग स्थल होना अनिवार्य है।

questions.question_english: During the recruitment of clerical staff in a government educational institution, a vacancy reserved for a person with benchmark disability remains unfilled due to the non-availability of a suitable candidate. What is the mandatory immediate procedural step under Section 34(2) of the RPwD Act, 2016?
options_english: The vacancy must be immediately de-reserved and filled by a general (unreserved) candidate in that cycle
The vacancy must be carried forward to the succeeding recruitment year as a backlog vacancy
The vacancy must be permanently converted into an SC or ST reserved vacancy
The recruitment process must be completely cancelled and the post permanently abolished
questions.explanation_english:
Section 34(2) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 explicitly establishes the procedure for unfilled reserved vacancies:
'Where in any recruitment year any vacancy cannot be filled up under sub-section (1) due to non-availability of a suitable person with benchmark disability or for any other sufficient reasons, such vacancy shall be carried forward in the succeeding recruitment year...'

The statute further provides that if in the succeeding recruitment year also a suitable candidate from that specific category is unavailable, the vacancy may first be filled by interchange among the five specified disability categories. Only when there is no person with disability available even after interchange can the post be filled by appointing a person other than a person with disability. Therefore, the immediate mandatory procedural step is to carry forward the vacancy to the next recruitment year; immediate de-reservation is strictly prohibited.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 34(2) में रिक्त पदों को भरने की सुस्पष्ट प्रक्रिया विहित की गई है:
'यदि किसी भर्ती वर्ष में उपधारा (1) के अधीन कोई रिक्ति उपयुक्त बेंचमार्क दिव्यांग व्यक्ति के उपलब्ध न होने के कारण अथवा किसी अन्य पर्याप्त कारण से नहीं भरी जा सकती है, तो ऐसी रिक्ति को आगामी भर्ती वर्ष में अग्रेषित (carried forward) किया जाएगा...'

कानून आगे यह प्रावधान करता है कि यदि आगामी भर्ती वर्ष में भी उस विशिष्ट दिव्यांगता श्रेणी का उपयुक्त अभ्यर्थी नहीं मिलता है, तो इसे पहले दिव्यांगता की अन्य श्रेणियों के बीच परस्पर बदलकर (interchange) भरा जाएगा। यदि इंटरचेंज के बाद भी कोई दिव्यांग व्यक्ति उपलब्ध नहीं होता है, केवल तभी उस पद पर गैर-दिव्यांग व्यक्ति की नियुक्ति की जा सकती है। अतः तात्कालिक अनिवार्य कदम उस रिक्ति को अगले वर्ष के लिए अग्रेषित (carry forward) करना है; रिक्ति का तत्काल अनारक्षण (de-reservation) पूरी तरह प्रतिबंधित है।

options_english: Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955

questions.explanation_english: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (POA Act), as amended in 2015, is a specialized criminal legislation enacted to prevent offenses and atrocities against members of SC and ST communities. Specifically, Section 3(1)(r) of the Act prescribes stringent penal consequences for anyone (not being a member of an SC or ST) who intentionally insults or intimidates with intent to humiliate a member of a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe in any place within public view. Educational institutions, including government, aided, or private schools, playgrounds, corridors, and classrooms accessible to peers or public, constitute places 'within public view'. The Act provides for specialized Special Courts, non-bailable arrest provisions, and mandatory compensation for victims. In the context of school administration, school heads and teachers must ensure zero tolerance for caste-based abuses, pejorative remarks, or discriminatory behavior, as failure to report or active participation attracts criminal culpability under this Act.
questions.explanation_hindi: अनुसूचित जाति और अनुसूचित जनजाति (अत्याचार निवारण) अधिनियम, 1989 (SC/ST Act) की धारा 3(1)(r) [2015 संशोधन के अनुसार] यह स्पष्ट प्रावधान करती है कि यदि कोई व्यक्ति, जो अनुसूचित जाति या अनुसूचित जनजाति का सदस्य नहीं है, किसी SC या ST सदस्य को 'सार्वजनिक दृष्टिगोचर' (Public view) किसी भी स्थान पर अपमानित करने के आशय से जानबूझकर अपमानित या भयभीत करता है, तो वह एक संज्ञेय और गैर-जमानती अपराध करता है। विद्यालय परिसर, खेल का मैदान, कक्षाएं और गलियारे कानूनी रूप से 'सार्वजनिक दृष्टिगोचर स्थान' के दायरे में आते हैं। विद्यालय प्रमुखों एवं शिक्षकों पर यह कानूनी दायित्व है कि वे परिसर में किसी भी प्रकार के जाति-आधारित ताने, मौखिक दुर्व्यवहार अथवा अपमानजनक व्यवहार को रोकें। ऐसा न करने पर संबंधित कर्मचारियों व अधिकारियों के विरुद्ध भी कठोर दंडात्मक कार्रवाई की जा सकती है। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: Article 16(4B) was inserted into the Constitution of India to safeguard the 'carry forward' rule for unfilled reserved vacancies. Under this constitutional provision, carried-forward (backlog) vacancies:
options_english: Are clubbed with the current year's vacancies and strictly subjected to the 50% reservation ceiling
Are treated as a distinct class of vacancies that are not subject to the 50% reservation ceiling in the succeeding year(s)
Lapse automatically if they remain unfilled across two consecutive recruitment cycles
Are immediately de-reserved and converted into open unreserved category vacancies in that cycle
questions.explanation_english:
Article 16(4B) was inserted into the Constitution by the Constitution (Eighty-First Amendment) Act, 2000. It was enacted to undo the rigid application of the 50% ceiling rule established in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), which had restricted the filling of backlog reserved vacancies if the total reservations in a given recruitment year exceeded 50%.

Article 16(4B) explicitly states:
'Nothing in this article shall prevent the State from considering any unfilled vacancies of a year which are reserved for being filled up in that year in accordance with any provision for reservation made under clause (4) or clause (4A) as a separate class of vacancies to be filled up in any succeeding year or years and such class of vacancies shall not be considered together with the vacancies of the year in which they are being filled up for determining the ceiling of fifty per cent reservation on total number of vacancies of that year.'

Operational significance for school administration and appointing authorities:
When calculating vacancies in a recruitment cycle, backlog vacancies of SC, ST, and OBC categories from previous years are segregated into a separate class. The 50% quota ceiling applies strictly to the current year's vacancies, while backlog vacancies can be filled 100% without violating the constitutional ceiling.
questions.explanation_hindi:
संविधान (81वां संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2000 द्वारा भारतीय संविधान में अनुच्छेद 16(4B) अंतःस्थापित किया गया था। इसका उद्देश्य इंद्रा साहनी (1992) मामले में प्रतिपादित 50% आरक्षण सीमा के उस कठोर प्रभाव को समाप्त करना था, जिसके कारण पिछले वर्षों की आरक्षित बैकलॉग रिक्तियों को भरने पर कुल आरक्षण 50% से अधिक हो जाने पर रोक लग जाती थी।

अनुच्छेद 16(4B) में स्पष्ट रूप से प्रावधान है:
राज्य किसी वर्ष की उन रिक्तियों को, जो अनुच्छेद 16(4) या 16(4A) के तहत आरक्षित थीं किंतु भरी नहीं जा सकीं, किसी आगामी वर्ष या वर्षों में भरे जाने के लिए 'रिक्तियों के एक पृथक वर्ग' के रूप में मान सकेगा और ऐसे रिक्तियों के वर्ग को उस वर्ष की कुल रिक्तियों पर 50% आरक्षण की अधिकतम सीमा की गणना करते समय चालू वर्ष की रिक्तियों के साथ नहीं जोड़ा जाएगा।

शैक्षिक प्रशासन और भर्ती प्राधिकारियों के लिए व्यावहारिक महत्व:
भर्ती चक्र में रोस्टर तैयार करते समय पिछले वर्षों की SC, ST और OBC की बैकलॉग रिक्तियों को अलग श्रेणी में रखा जाता है। 50% की सीमा केवल चालू वर्ष (नियमित) की रिक्तियों पर लागू होती है, जबकि बैकलॉग रिक्तियों को शत-प्रतिशत आरक्षित पदों के रूप में भरा जा सकता है।

questions.explanation_english: In special and inclusive education, IEP stands for Individualized Education Program (or Individualized Education Plan). It is a legally binding, customized, and structured instructional document developed collaboratively by a multidisciplinary team—comprising general classroom teachers, special educators, school counselors, speech/occupational therapists, the school principal, and the child's parents. The IEP details the child's present levels of academic and functional performance (PLAAFP), establishes measurable annual learning goals and short-term benchmarks, specifies required pedagogical accommodations and curricular modifications, identifies needed assistive technology, and outlines periodic progress monitoring schedules tailored to the unique learning pace of the child.
questions.explanation_hindi: समावेशी एवं विशेष शिक्षा के क्षेत्र में IEP का पूर्ण रूप 'इंडिविजुअलाइज्ड एजुकेशन प्रोग्राम' (Individualized Education Program - व्यक्तिगत शिक्षण कार्यक्रम) है। यह एक बहुविषयक टीम (जिसमें सामान्य शिक्षक, विशेष शिक्षक, परामर्शदाता, स्कूल प्रधानाचार्य और बच्चे के माता-पिता शामिल होते हैं) द्वारा तैयार किया गया एक व्यक्तिगत व सुनियोजित शैक्षणिक दस्तावेज़ होता है। IEP में दिव्यांग बच्चे के सीखने के वर्तमान स्तर का मूल्यांकन, उसके लिए निर्धारित अल्पकालिक एवं वार्षिक मापनीय लक्ष्य, आवश्यक कक्षा समायोजन (Accommodations), पाठ्यचर्या संशोधन (Modifications), आवश्यक सहायक उपकरण तथा प्रगति मूल्यांकन की समय-सीमा दर्ज होती है, जिससे बच्चे की विशिष्ट क्षमताओं के अनुरूप उसका सर्वांगीण विकास हो सके।

questions.question_english: A Class VIII student in a Delhi Government school exhibits extreme difficulty in coordinating muscle movements required for speaking and writing. The medical certificate indicates an injury to the brain that occurred before birth. Under which specified disability category of the RPwD Act, 2016 does this fall?

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 1(A)(c) of the Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 'Cerebral Palsy' is classified under Locomotor Disability and is defined as a non-progressive condition characterized by abnormal motor control posture resulting from brain insult or injuries occurring in the pre-natal, peri-natal, or infant period of development. The clinical indicators presented in the question—extreme difficulty in muscle coordination affecting speech and writing arising from brain injury occurring before birth (pre-natal)—precisely match the legal definition of Cerebral Palsy. In inclusive schools, students with cerebral palsy are legally entitled under Section 16 to assistive speech tech, adapted furniture, mobility devices, scribes, and compensatory exam time.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की अनुसूची के भाग 1(A)(c) के अनुसार, 'प्रमस्तिष्कीय घात' (Cerebral Palsy) को चलन दिव्यांगता के अंतर्गत वर्गीकृत किया गया है। इसे जन्म से पूर्व (pre-natal), जन्म के दौरान या शैशवावस्था में मस्तिष्क को हुई क्षति के कारण उत्पन्न मोटर नियंत्रण और मुद्रा की गैर-प्रगतिशील स्थिति के रूप में परिभाषित किया गया है। प्रश्न में प्रस्तुत लक्षण (जन्म से पूर्व मस्तिष्क क्षति के कारण बोलने और लिखने में मांसपेशियों के समन्वय में गंभीर समस्या) पूर्णतः सेरेब्रल पाल्सी की वैधानिक परिभाषा से मेल खाते हैं। समावेशी शिक्षा के तहत धारा 16 के अनुसार विद्यालय ऐसे विद्यार्थियों को सहायक उपकरण, सुलभ बैठने की व्यवस्था और परीक्षा में प्रतिपूरक समय व लेखक उपलब्ध कराने के लिए बाध्य हैं।

questions.explanation_english: According to the National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration (NIEPA) National Centre for School Leadership (NCSL) frameworks, an effective School Principal must function as an 'Inclusive Leader'. Inclusive leadership requires institutional heads to move beyond token compliance and actively cultivate a school-wide culture that values equity, empathy, and neurodiversity. The Principal is directly responsible for eliminating structural barriers (ensuring ramps, tactile floorings, barrier-free toilets, and accessible drinking water), facilitating collaboration between regular teachers and special educators, overseeing the formulation and execution of Individualized Education Programs (IEPs), and ensuring that no child is segregated, excluded, or denied full participation in co-curricular and scholastic school life.

questions.question_english: Can a Government establishment be exempted from the mandatory provision of reserving vacancies for persons with benchmark disabilities under the RPwD Act, 2016?
options_english: No, reservation in public employment is an absolute statutory right and no establishment can be exempted under any circumstances

questions.explanation_english:
While Section 34(1) of the RPwD Act, 2016 mandates a minimum 4% reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities in every Government establishment, the first proviso to Section 34(1) expressly provides for exemptions:
'Provided that the appropriate Government may, having regard to the type of work carried on in any department or establishment, by notification and subject to such conditions, if any, as may be specified in such notification, exempt any establishment from the provisions of this section.'

Such exemption cannot be granted arbitrarily or by an individual Head of Department; it requires an official gazette notification by the appropriate Government (Central or State Government), typically in consultation with the Chief Commissioner or State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (e.g., combatant units of armed forces or paramilitary forces).
questions.explanation_hindi:
यद्यपि RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 34(1) प्रत्येक सरकारी प्रतिष्ठान में बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगजनों के लिए 4% आरक्षण अनिवार्य करती है, परंतु धारा 34(1) का प्रथम परंतुक (proviso) विशिष्ट छूट का अधिकार देता है:
'परंतु समुचित सरकार किसी विभाग या प्रतिष्ठान में किए जाने वाले कार्य के प्रकार को ध्यान में रखते हुए, अधिसूचना द्वारा तथा ऐसी शर्तों के अधीन, किसी भी प्रतिष्ठान को इस धारा के प्रावधानों से छूट दे सकती है।'

यह विधिक छूट किसी विभागाध्यक्ष के व्यक्तिगत विवेक पर निर्भर नहीं होती, बल्कि केवल समुचित सरकार (केंद्र या राज्य सरकार) द्वारा विधिवत गजट अधिसूचना जारी करके ही दी जा सकती है (जैसे सशस्त्र बलों या अर्धसैनिक बलों के लड़ाकू संवर्गों के लिए)।
